component.name: RatClick
component.summary: Click the mouse for you, at a rate and for a time you choose

description.p: RatClick is an auto-clicker for GNOME. Pick a click rate, a mouse button and how long the run should last, then start it from the window, from a global keyboard shortcut, or from the command line.

ul.li: Clicks per minute from a slow tap to a fast burst
Endless runs, or a timed run that stops itself
A global toggle shortcut through GNOME, the bundled Shell extension, or keyd
A Quick Settings toggle and panel indicator, through the bundled GNOME Shell extension
A background service on the session bus, so the shortcut works without the window open
A scriptable command line, including machine-readable status output

description.p: The clicks come from a virtual pointer created through the kernel uinput device, so they work the same under Wayland and X11. You need to be in the input group; the bundled diagnostic command tells you whether you already are.
Fixes a missing icon on the setup wizard's final page and beside every passing check in the diagnostics view, on systems without the legacy Adwaita icon theme installed.
Adds a visual effect at the pointer when clicking starts or stops, drawn by the GNOME Shell extension and configurable per direction.
The configuration file can now be opened in an editor with ratclick config, and is validated before it is accepted.
Adds a reset that undoes every setting and shortcut, and asks for administrator rights when the keyd backend needs them instead of failing.
